statements.status_notes: CVE-2024-26461 is a memory leak in lib/gssapi/krb5/k5sealv3.c, the GSSAPI per-message seal/unseal path in libgssapi-krb5-2, with no fix planned by Debian. The leaking code runs only inside an established GSS-API security context. In this image GSSAPI is reachable only through libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit when an operator explicitly configures SASL/GSSAPI (Kerberos) for the Kafka event source or an ingestion source against their own KDC and brokers; the image binds no GSSAPI-authenticated listener (the framework is a Kafka client and GMS REST client, verified package set and entrypoint on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image). An unauthenticated adversary has no channel to feed GSS tokens to this code; per-message tokens arrive only from operator-trusted brokers inside an operator-established security context, so the leak cannot be driven by an adversary.

CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c, the ONC RPC portmapper helper in libgssrpc, with no fix planned by Debian. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: libgssrpc.so.4 is present only as a dependency of the krb5-user kadmin/kpasswd client tools; no long-running process links it. The entrypoint chain (start.sh -> python datahub-actions, plus the JRE only inside the executor's ingest subprocess on full variants) never loads libgssrpc and the image binds no RPC listener, so the leaking path runs only when an operator interactively invokes kadmin.mit against an admin server they chose. An adversary has no channel to drive the leak, and a memory leak in a short-lived operator-invoked CLI yields no denial-of-service leverage.

CVE-2018-5709 is an integer truncation of dbentry->n_key_data in kadmin/dbutil/dump.c, code that compiles into the kdb5_util KDC database tool shipped by Debian's krb5-kdc/krb5-admin-server packages. This image installs only krb5-config, krb5-user and the MIT runtime libraries. Verified on the built dhi/datahub-actions:1.5.0.7-debian13 image: kdb5_util, kadmind and krb5kdc exist in neither /usr/bin nor /usr/sbin (only the krb5-user client tools such as kinit.mit, klist.mit and kadmin.mit ship), so the vulnerable database-dump code is not present.

Integer underflow and heap out-of-bounds read in berval2tl_data() in the LDAP KDB backend plugin (plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ldap_principal2.c). Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. Debian marks this unimportant (bug 1139821) with no security impact and notes it does not cross any security boundary.

Triggering requires a KDC or kadmind configured with an LDAP database backend whose backend returns a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2; that data originates from the trusted KDB datastore, not from an external Kerberos protocol client, so it cannot be controlled by an adversary. CVE-2024-26461 is a memory leak in lib/gssapi/krb5/k5sealv3.c, on an error path that upstream notes cannot be triggered through GSSAPI API calls with attacker input. datahub-ingestion uses GSSAPI purely as a client when a recipe enables Kerberos authentication; a remote peer cannot drive the leaking error path, and Debian marks the issue unimportant with negligible security impact and ships no fixed version for trixie. The process is a short-lived one-shot ingestion CLI, so even a triggered leak would be bounded by the process lifetime and have no security consequence.

CVE-2024-26458 is a memory leak in lib/rpc/pmap_rmt.c, the legacy SunRPC portmapper broadcast client inside libgssrpc. The image ships libgssrpc only as a dependency of the kadmin client utilities; nothing in datahub-ingestion issues portmapper broadcast RPCs. Kerberos use here is client-side GSSAPI/SASL authentication through libgssapi-krb5-2 (libsasl2-modules-gssapi-mit) against operator-configured sources, which never enters the pmap_rmt code, so an adversary has no input channel into the leaking path. Debian marks the leak unimportant with negligible security impact and ships no fixed version for trixie; the process is additionally a short-lived one-shot CLI where a bounded leak has no security effect.

CVE-2018-5709 is an integer truncation in kadmin/dbutil/dump.c (dbentry->n_key_data assigned from a 32-bit value), code that compiles into the kdb5_util KDC database dump utility shipped in Debian's krb5-kdc/krb5-admin-server packages. This image installs only the client-side Kerberos packages (krb5-user, krb5-config, libkrb5-3, libkrb5support0, libgssapi-krb5-2) needed for Kerberos-authenticated ingestion sources. Verified in the built image: no kdb5_util or any KDC/kadmin-server tooling exists on the filesystem (only client binaries such as kadmin.mit/kinit.mit are present), so the vulnerable dump code is not shipped. Debian additionally marks the issue unimportant because the dump path only ever processes the KDC's own trusted database.
